The '''Language Restoration Act of 1950''' was a post-independence Belcantese law that restored the [[Belcantese Language]] to official public use and created the [[Belcantese Language Institute]].

== Background ==

Vesperan occupation had restricted Belcantese language institutions and promoted [[Vesperan Language|Vesperan]] in government, education, and public culture. After independence, language policy became one of the new republic's first reconstruction priorities.

== Provisions ==

The act established a national language authority, restored Belcantese in public administration and education, and supported the development of modern terminology for government, technology, diplomacy, law, and reconstruction.

== Legacy ==

The act linked cultural restoration to state-building. It treated Belcantese not only as heritage but as a working language of the postwar [[Belcanto Nations]].
